_note: Fix-now register for ongoing clients. type: remove | stop | rewrite | disclose | verify. basis: 'doc' = the document states the underlying rule; 'interp' = our interpretation or recommended practice (shown with a label). No urgency field by design.

actions.check: Patient testimonial pages, sliders, quote blocks and “what patients say” sections
actions.wrong: Testimonials are prohibited. Patient consent does not change that.
actions.how: Unpublish the page or module. Remove its menu and footer links. 301-redirect the old URL to a relevant factual page. Take it out of sitemaps and internal links.

actions.check: Video testimonials (website, YouTube, reels, ad creatives)
actions.wrong: Patient video endorsements are prohibited, and the patient is identifiable.
actions.how: Unpublish or set to private. Pull from ad accounts and playlists. Keep the raw files archived for the client, but do not reuse.

actions.check: Before-and-after galleries, “Results” pages, transformation carousels and sliders
actions.wrong: Before-and-after photographs and surgical results are prohibited. Consent does not fix this.
actions.how: Remove the page, module and menu links. Redirect the URL. Remove from ad assets and social highlights. Do not repurpose them into “case study” posts.
actions.keep: The only stated exception is anonymised scientific or educational publication with consent. Escalate to Leadership before using it (see grey areas).

actions.check: Superlatives in headlines, hero text, titles, meta descriptions, GBP descriptions and ad copy: “best”, “No.1”, “leading”, “most trusted”, “top”, “unmatched”
actions.wrong: Superiority claims are barred unless objectively verifiable with an independent, transparent methodology.
actions.how: Replace with neutral, factual wording about what the clinic offers and where. Search and replace across all templates, titles, schema and ad assets.

actions.check: Any superlative the client says is verifiable (for example, a ranking from a named, published study)
actions.wrong: A claim is only allowed if objectively verifiable, with a transparent, independently ascertainable methodology.
actions.how: Get the source, methodology, date and awarding body in writing. Leadership signs off. If it cannot be shown, treat it as A04.

actions.check: Patient counters, “10,000+ patients treated”, success-rate stats, satisfaction percentages
actions.wrong: Success rates and number of patients treated are named in the prohibition.
actions.how: Delete the counter or stat block, including in structured data and ad assets. Use factual descriptions of services instead.

actions.check: “Guaranteed”, “100% success”, “painless”, “miracle”, “exclusive cure”, and similar absolute words
actions.wrong: These phrases are named in the document as examples of prohibited claims.
actions.how: Rewrite to describe the procedure and its usual process and risks. Do not replace them with a softer synonym that means the same thing.

actions.check: “Permanent results”, “instant results”, “risk-free”, “no side effects”, “safe for everyone”
actions.wrong: Likely to create unrealistic expectations, misrepresent outcomes or conceal risks.
actions.how: Replace with balanced wording that states that results vary and risks exist, as confirmed by the doctor.

actions.check: Doctor identity block: name, qualifications, registration status, SMR/NMR number
actions.wrong: Electronic posts must show these details. Many sites and landing pages show only a name and degree.
actions.how: Add the block to the doctor profile, to the site footer, and to landing pages. Collect the numbers from the client first and have the client confirm them in writing.
actions.keep: Where on the page the details must appear is not specified. Our placement is an interpretation.

actions.check: Blog posts and articles: author byline and doctor identity
actions.wrong: Posts published under a doctor's name, or on a clinic site, need identity and registration details. Agency-written posts with no doctor review also carry risk.
actions.how: Add a byline block with name, qualifications, registration status and SMR/NMR number. Record that the doctor reviewed the post.

actions.check: Award and ranking badges, “Featured in…” strips, “Top 10” lists
actions.wrong: Awards and rankings must be independently verifiable, with methodology, date and awarding body disclosed where needed.
actions.how: Collect proof for each badge. Remove any pay-to-feature, nomination-fee or unverifiable badge. Where kept, add awarding body, year and basis.

actions.check: Comparison to other clinics or doctors (“better than…”, “unlike other clinics…”, “unmatched”)
actions.wrong: Comparative and superiority claims are barred unless objectively verifiable.
actions.how: Delete the comparison and rewrite the sentence as a neutral statement of what the clinic offers.

actions.check: Dynamic keyword insertion (DKI) in Google Ads headlines
actions.wrong: DKI can insert “best”, “top” or “cheap” from keywords into the ad text, which would put restricted claims in the ad.
actions.how: Switch DKI off. Use static headlines approved by the client. Audit the keyword list for restricted terms.
actions.keep: The document does not mention DKI. This is our reading of the risk.

actions.check: Ad headlines, descriptions and callouts with superlatives, guarantees, results or success claims
actions.wrong: Ads are advertisements under §3.2, and the same claim rules apply.
actions.how: Rewrite in factual form: service, location, how to contact, fees if shown. Get written client approval before they go live.

actions.check: Google review, seller-rating and star-rating extensions or callouts in ads
actions.wrong: Using reviews and ratings to promote services is a testimonial or endorsement risk.
actions.how: Remove review-based assets and callouts such as “4.9 stars”. Ask the client to confirm.
actions.keep: The review rule in §3.2 Expl. V is explicit about fake or paid reviews and about social media. Applying it to ad extensions is our conservative reading.

actions.check: Image assets and sitelinks that point to results, testimonials, offers or before-and-after content
actions.wrong: They promote content that is itself prohibited.
actions.how: Remove the asset or sitelink. Replace with factual images (clinic, equipment) and links to factual pages.

actions.check: Offer, discount, coupon, promotion and price-drop assets; “limited period”, “festive offer”, “free procedure”
actions.wrong: Discounts, limited-period offers, coupons and free procedures are listed inducements.
actions.how: Pause and remove promotion assets and offer posts. Replace with a factual statement of fees where the client wants one.

actions.check: “Free consultation” and “free check-up” wording
actions.wrong: “Free” procedures are named. Whether a free consultation is a prohibited inducement is not clear from the text.
actions.how: Take it to Leadership. Until answered, do not introduce new “free” offers and record client approval for any that remain.

actions.check: Ad-to-landing-page match: where do live ads land?
actions.wrong: An ad that lands on a page with testimonials, before-and-after, superlatives or offers carries that exposure.
actions.how: List every ad's destination URL. Pause ads that point to affected pages until those pages are fixed. Re-point to compliant pages.

actions.check: Fear-based or urgency hooks in ads, posts and reels (“before it's too late”, “don't ignore this”)
actions.wrong: Fear-based marketing and creating unnecessary demand are listed prohibitions.
actions.how: Rewrite to inform calmly: what the condition is, when to see a doctor, with no alarm.
actions.keep: Do not delete educational content. Fix the hook, not the topic.

actions.check: Meta ad creatives: before-and-after, patient faces, results, testimonial quotes
actions.wrong: Prohibited content under §8.1(v), §3.2 Expl. V and §7.4.
actions.how: Pause ads, remove creatives and rebuild from approved factual or educational assets.

actions.check: Meta lead-gen forms and ads with offers, “limited slots”, giveaways, contests
actions.wrong: Contests, gifts and limited-period offers are listed inducements.
actions.how: Remove the offer text. Keep a neutral “contact us” or “book an appointment” form if the client approves.

actions.check: Influencer, celebrity, creator and staff collaborations; branded-content tags
actions.wrong: Endorsements by celebrities, influencers, patients and employees are barred, and a third party must not do what the clinic cannot.
actions.how: Pause active collaborations and any paid partnership ads. No new ones without Leadership sign-off.

actions.check: Custom audiences, lookalikes, remarketing lists and CRM uploads built from patient or enquiry data
actions.wrong: Personal data used in advertising must follow the IT Act and the DPDP Act. Health-related enquiry data is sensitive.
actions.how: List all audiences and data sources. Confirm consent and privacy notice with the client. Delete audiences that have no documented basis.

actions.check: Reshared reviews, review screenshots, Google-review graphics, “patient love” posts, testimonial stories
actions.wrong: A doctor must not request or share patient testimonials or reviews for professional promotion on social media.
actions.how: Delete the posts and clear them from Highlights, pinned posts and playlists.

actions.check: Before-and-after reels, transformation posts, “result of the week” posts
actions.wrong: Before-and-after and surgical results are prohibited.
actions.how: Delete the posts and reels. Remove from Highlights and cross-posts.

actions.check: Clinic reels and photos with patients visible: faces, names, tattoos, birthmarks, chat screenshots
actions.wrong: Identifiable patient data must not be shared. Consent must be documented, and identifying details blurred or cropped.
actions.how: Review every piece of footage with people in it. Remove where consent is not documented or where the use is promotional. Blur or crop where a lawful use remains.

actions.check: Festival offers, giveaways, contests, referral campaigns on social
actions.wrong: Listed inducements.
actions.how: Delete the posts and stop running similar campaigns. Keep purely factual greetings under §8.2(v).

actions.check: Celebrity-patient mentions, collab posts, “as seen on” and media features
actions.wrong: Publicising celebrity patients is prohibited, and endorsements are barred.
actions.how: Remove celebrity patient mentions. Media features need a separate check: see grey areas.

actions.check: AI-generated images, videos, avatars, voice-overs and AI-written copy
actions.wrong: Synthetic patients, doctors, voices and outcomes are prohibited. Other AI promotional content needs a source mark.
actions.how: Inventory all AI-assisted assets. Remove any that depict people, voices or results. Label the rest as AI-generated.

actions.check: Social profiles and posts: doctor name, qualifications and registration number visible
actions.wrong: Electronic media posts must disclose these details.
actions.how: Add to the profile bio or About section and in captions where the doctor features. Have the client confirm the numbers.
actions.keep: Where the details appear for social posts is our interpretation.

actions.check: Doctor-to-camera scripts with claims: “I'm the best”, “I've done 5,000 surgeries”, “guaranteed”
actions.wrong: Personal achievements, patient numbers and absolute claims are prohibited.
actions.how: Re-cut the edit or re-shoot. Rewrite scripts for education, not self-promotion.

actions.check: Planned shoots with patient interviews, patient walkthroughs and procedure footage
actions.wrong: Patient testimonials and promotional patient stories are prohibited. Procedure footage raises consent and live-surgery questions.
actions.how: Cancel or reshape. Shoot the doctor explaining a topic, the clinic, equipment and facilities. Check procedure footage against §7.5 first.

actions.check: Doctor shown recommending a skincare, haircare, device or supplement brand
actions.wrong: No endorsement of any drug, device or health product linked to the doctor's name or face, paid or not.
actions.how: Delete the clip or post. Remove brand tie-ins.

actions.check: Live procedures, surgery reels or live-stream footage
actions.wrong: Live surgery and commercial dissemination of procedures must follow NMC's live-surgery framework. We do not have it.
actions.how: Pause new procedure content until the client confirms the applicable framework and consent in writing.

actions.check: Educational blogs and articles: check for promotional character, not for deletion
actions.wrong: Non-promotional information is exempt. A post that pushes the clinic, makes claims or has booking calls to action may count as advertising.
actions.how: Keep the post. Take out superlatives, results, offers and heavy sales calls to action. Add the doctor byline. Keep a plain contact block.

actions.check: Case-study and “patient journey” posts
actions.wrong: Publishing cases for promotion and personal success stories is prohibited.
actions.how: Remove patient stories. Journal-published research can be summarised: see A38.

actions.check: Posts summarising research the doctor has published in a reputed journal
actions.wrong: Allowed as research-based communication, but it must be genuinely that.
actions.how: Link to the journal article. Confirm authorship with the client. No patient imagery or promotional tone.

actions.check: Medical claims in articles and service pages: cure, timelines, session counts, efficacy statements
actions.wrong: Statements about outcomes and efficacy must be evidence-based and not create unrealistic expectations or hide risks.
actions.how: Ask the client's doctor to confirm each claim and cite a source. Rewrite or remove any claim without support.

actions.check: AI-written blogs and service copy
actions.wrong: AI-assisted content must not mislead on diagnosis, outcomes or services. AI promotional content needs a source mark.
actions.how: Have the client's doctor review. Fix or remove unverified statements. Add an AI source mark where the content is AI-generated promotional content.

actions.check: Service pages: outcome promises, “permanent”, timelines, “works in X sessions”
actions.wrong: Outcome claims can be unrealistic, unverifiable or hide risks.
actions.how: Describe the procedure, who it may suit, usual process and known risks. Remove timelines and guarantees.

actions.check: Device and technology pages: “most advanced”, “latest”, “FDA-approved” and accuracy claims
actions.wrong: Equipment may be mentioned as a fact. Superiority, guaranteed accuracy or outcomes are not allowed. Regulatory status claims must be true.
actions.how: State the device name and what it is used for. Remove superiority language. Verify any regulatory approval claim with the client and the manufacturer.

actions.check: Pricing, package and “offer” pages
actions.wrong: Fee disclosure is allowed if factual and not misleading. Offer and discount framing is not.
actions.how: Show fees plainly, with what is included. Remove “festival price”, “flat X% off” and countdown timers.

actions.check: Doctor profile pages: “renowned”, “celebrity doctor”, patient counts, awards, glowing bios
actions.wrong: Achievements, patient numbers and superiority terms are prohibited. A doctor bio must not become promotional portrayal.
actions.how: Rewrite as a factual bio: qualifications, registration, specialties, memberships, place of practice.

actions.check: Doctor photos on hero banners, ads, signage, letterhead and social creatives
actions.wrong: A doctor's photograph is not permitted where it is self-advertisement or promotional publicity. The line between promotional and informational is not defined.
actions.how: Take to Leadership. Until answered, avoid new doctor-photo hero banners and ad creatives. A photo beside a factual directory entry is lower risk.

actions.check: Title tags and meta descriptions with superlatives, patient counts or claims
actions.wrong: Search-engine content is advertising when promotional, and the same claim rules apply.
actions.how: Rewrite the titles and descriptions of all pages. Use factual terms: service, specialty, location.

actions.check: Google Business Profile: description, posts, offers, Q&A and services
actions.wrong: A GBP is a listing that promotes the clinic. Offers and claims in it are in scope.
actions.how: Limit to name, address, hours, services, facilities, fees and doctor details. Remove offer posts, claims and photos of results.

actions.check: Review requests: QR codes, WhatsApp and SMS review links, front-desk scripts, review incentives, review gating
actions.wrong: No soliciting reviews, and no purchase, procurement or manipulation of them.
actions.how: Stop review campaigns and remove QR codes, scripts and incentives. Tell the client in writing.
actions.keep: Whether a passive, neutral feedback link is allowed is unclear. See grey areas.

actions.check: Purchased, fake or staff-written reviews; bought followers, likes or comments; engagement pods
actions.wrong: Prohibited, including through a third party.
actions.how: Stop immediately. Report any found to the client and Leadership. Request removal where possible.

actions.check: Public replies to reviews: do they confirm a patient, treatment or outcome?
actions.wrong: Replies that reveal patient identity or treatment details share identifiable patient data.
actions.how: Use a generic reply with no names, treatment or outcome details. Move the conversation offline.
actions.keep: The document does not address review replies. This is our interpretation.

actions.check: Embedded review widgets, star-rating badges and review sliders on the website
actions.wrong: Showing reviews to promote services is a testimonial risk.
actions.how: Remove the widgets and badges from all templates.
actions.keep: §3.2 Expl. V names social media for sharing reviews. Applying it to a website is our conservative reading.

actions.check: Structured data: aggregateRating and Review markup on clinic pages
actions.wrong: It exists to show star ratings in search results, which promotes reviews.
actions.how: Remove Review and AggregateRating schema. Keep organisation, physician and local business details that are factual.

actions.check: Location and keyword pages named “Best [specialist] in [city]”
actions.wrong: The page presents a superiority claim.
actions.how: Rename to the factual form: “[Specialty] clinic in [city]”. Keep a factual description of services and facilities.
actions.keep: Users searching for “best…” is not itself a rule issue. The claim on our page is.

actions.check: Directory and platform listings: paid “featured”, “top-ranked”, sponsored placement
actions.wrong: Platforms must not rank doctors for payment. A doctor paying for a rank is a risk.
actions.how: List the platforms the client uses, and the plan and rank type on each. Cancel paid ranking.

actions.check: WhatsApp broadcasts and chatbots with offers, results, testimonials or doctor promotion
actions.wrong: WhatsApp is a named medium. The same rules apply.
actions.how: Pause the broadcasts. Re-write to factual updates only, to people who opted in.

actions.check: Email newsletters and drip sequences
actions.wrong: Promotional emails fall under the claim, offer and testimonial rules, and use personal data.
actions.how: Remove offers, results and superlatives. Check consent and unsubscribe.

actions.check: Print, hoardings, flyers and brochures
actions.wrong: Hoardings may carry only factual infrastructure and facility information. Pamphlets must make no superiority or unsubstantiated claims.
actions.how: Rework to facts only. Remove doctor photos, results and slogans with superlatives.

actions.check: Paid news, advertorials, PR placements and “doctor interview” articles
actions.wrong: News articles intended for promotion are a named medium, and third parties cannot do what the doctor cannot.
actions.how: Stop paid editorial placements. Public-health talks in the doctor's own name may continue: see §8.2(iii).

actions.check: Our own pricing models: any fee linked to patients, bookings or leads delivered
actions.wrong: Agency payment must not be structured so it is linked to procuring or referring individual patients.
actions.how: Leadership reviews every client contract and invoice model. Do not change terms until advised.

actions.check: Written client approval of every change and every new deliverable
actions.wrong: The doctor is responsible for content they authorised or knowingly permitted. We need a record that they did.
actions.how: For each client, send the list of changes by email, and get a reply approving. Store it in the client folder.

actions.check: Website and landing-page forms, consent text, privacy policy and cookie banners
actions.wrong: Personal data used in advertising must follow the IT Act and the DPDP Act.
actions.how: Add a clear consent line and privacy link on every form.

actions.check: Accreditation, emergency-service and infrastructure claims
actions.wrong: Accreditation status and facilities may be shown only if factual and verifiable.
actions.how: Ask the client for certificates. Remove any claim that cannot be shown.

actions.check: “Years of experience” and “senior consultant” claims
actions.wrong: Not named in the prohibition. Still a personal achievement claim that must be verifiable.
actions.how: Confirm from registration and CV. Keep it factual. Note the open question on the grey-areas page.

actions.check: National-day and festival greeting posts
actions.wrong: Greetings are allowed on days of national or professional importance if they carry no promotion.
actions.how: Keep greetings plain. Remove offers, doctor-photo banners and booking calls to action from them.

actions.check: Platform AI features: generative image or text options in ad accounts and social tools
actions.wrong: Automatically AI-altered creative may not carry the required disclosure or may depict people or outcomes.
actions.how: Turn off automatic generative enhancements in ad accounts. Review any AI-generated variant before use.
